learning_outcomes.text: To know the general applications of systems theory in the industrial field and understand automatic control as one of the main applications.
To understand and know how to appropriately use the terminology of the subject (signals, systems, transforms, transfer functions).
To know how to calculate direct and inverse Laplace and Z transforms.
To know the practical application of Fourier, Laplace, and Z transforms in systems theory.
To obtain the transfer functions of continuous and discrete systems from their differential equations and difference equations, respectively.
To model continuous and discrete systems, as well as delays in systems.
To analyze the stability of continuous and discrete systems.
To analyze the dynamic behavior of continuous and discrete systems.
To identify continuous systems from their temporal response to input signals.
To apply the studied modeling and analysis techniques for systems of interest in engineering (electrical, thermal, hydraulic) and, in particular, mechanical systems.

syllabus_topics: Modeling of discrete and sampled systems.
Stability and dynamic behavior of systems.

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical-practical exam (theory part in the classroom and practical part in the laboratory)

assessment_rules: A theoretical-practical exam will be conducted, evaluating theory, problems, and practical skills. The exam will consist of problems, questions, and a practical exercise to be solved in the laboratory. Correction and scoring criteria for each problem will be indicated in the exam statement. Assignments on specific course topics may be submitted. The teaching staff may request an oral explanation of the resolution, practical exercise, or submitted work as part of the assessment.
